model_annotations.Bulgarian: The graph is titled "Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-2" and represents three different scenarios of sparsity ratios across different layers. The x-axis is labeled "Layer" with values ranging from 0 to 20, and the y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" with values ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. The dashed blue line represents the "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03." The dotted orange line represents the "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44." The dash-dot green line represents the "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33." The graph shows that the sparsity ratio before the gate is much lower than the sparsity ratio after the gate, and the sparsity ratio after the average gate is slightly lower than the average sparsity ratio after the gate but much higher than before the gate. The graph has no data points or markers indicated; it is a continuous line graph.
model_annotations.Chinese:
The graph displays the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers, with data points deriving from three distinct scenarios: before a gate, after a gate, and after averaging gates within 1e-2 units. In the x-axis, the layers range from 0 to 20. For the y-axis, the sparsity ratio varies from 0.0 to 1.0. The graphs are differentiated by line styles and colors: a dashed blue line represents the sparsity ratio before the gate with an average of 0.03, an orange dotted line shows the sparsity ratio after the gate with an average of 0.44, and a green dash-dot line indicates the sparsity ratio after averaging gates, averaging 0.33.

Each line exhibits different trends with respect to the number of layers. The sparsity ratio before the gate (blue dashed line) remains constant at 0.03, starting from the 0th layer. The after gate scenario (orange dotted line) shows a decrease initially till the fifth layer and maintains a value around 0.44. The after average gate line (green dash-dot line) displays a more fluctuating pattern but generally stays above a sparsity ratio of 0.2 as it moves from 5 to 20 layers. There are no discernible peaks or troughs that can be confidently identified for representations at specific layers. The graph is presented without any extrapolated predictions on trends.
model_annotations.English: The graph titled Sarsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-2 depicts the sparsity ratio of three different configurations—before gate, after gate, and after average gate—against various layers of a system or model. The x-axis is labeled "Layer" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20 with equal intervals, but the exact units are not specified. The y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" and also uses a linear scale, stretching from 0.0 to 1.0, again with equal intervals. There are three lines representing different sparsity ratios: the blue dashed line corresponds to the sparsity ratio before the gate with an average of 0.03; the orange dotted line represents the sparsity ratio after the gate with an average of 0.44; and the green dash-dot line shows the sparsity ratio after the average gate with an average of 0.33. Overall, the graph illustrates a decreasing trend in sparsity ratio as the number of layers increases. The blue dashed line starts close to a sparsity ratio of 1 and diminishes as the layer number rises. The orange dotted line begins slightly lower than the blue dashed line and also decreases but with fluctuating values, including a notable peak around layer 5, followed by a significant dip and another rise. The green dash-dot line starts similar to the other two lines but decreases more steeply before increasing slightly towards the last layers. This suggests that the gating mechanism affects the system's sparsity differently, with some configurations potentially allowing for more sparsity than others at different layers.
model_annotations.German: Das Bild ist eine Fluktuationsdichte-freie Gigant-Kompressionsleitung (SDPA) Zeichnung, die die Signifikanz von bestimmten Volumina/Predatoren (VNPs) in Wildwassernachhaltigkeit einbezieht. Das Diagramm illustriert zwei verschiedene Szenarien, während die x-Achse die Schichtzahl der Kontrolle (Lager) oder die Anzahl der unabhängigen Versickerungspfade mit VNPs darstellt. Die y-Achse entspricht der Analyse signifikanz, wobei 1.0 den höchsten Schätzungswert darstellt, die am linken Rand markiert sind, und eine aktuelle schätzte signifikanz die Nullschwelle ist. Das Bild besteht aus drei Linien, wobei jede Linie eine getrennte Analyse repräsentiert. Die erste durchweg gestrichelte Linie (dazu auf DR-8 verfolgend) stellt die Schätzungen vor nach einer Schätzung der Infektionsrate und resultierend darin, dass VNPs signifikant sind, dar, die eine kindbedungsbedingte Inzidenz von 0.004 beträgt. Im Diagramm ist die durchschnittliche signifikanz vor der Infektionsrate 0.03. Die zweite gestrichelte (orange) Linie stellt die Tabellenfortschreibung dar, in der die einfachste von 0.42. Die durchschnittliche signifikanz nach der Infektionsrate wird aus dieser Schätzung vorgegangen, heißt 0.44. Die dritte gestrichelte (grünes) Linie stellt die durchschnittlichen berechneten Angaben dar, im Fall des Grenzinfektionsrates von 0.33.
